No Customers
Feb 2017 • Couples
I have been watching the Niche since it opened, and one of the biggest issues is that it's in a western district serving below average food, i know because i have been there 10x, hoping that the menu would change.
The first thing you notice is the windows when you come to the niche, it has a christmas wreath painted across them, which carries on to the Glenwood. As you walk inside this very small bar is right in front of you which has limited drinks. They are quite expensive as well considering that you have local pubs very close by.
The inside of the restraunt is quite nice, but there is never anyone in it. The reason why no one is there is because of the menu, as they are not sure what types of food they are promoting. The bacon wrapped burger is ok, but 300 meters away the best burger in Vietnam is served at Fat shaggys. 600 meters in both directions you have great italians, and niche promotes vietnamese foods as well but this is a western district, and we are surrounded by vietnamese food, so why can they not focus on a western taste. 
As for the food, its ok but i have had to send things like chicken and steak back to the kitchen as it is undercooked. Chefs and staff need to go to other places to see how its run and how the food is.
Niche would be better to become a western grocery store and sell home made sandwiches and have a nice little tea/coffee room.

A regular for me
Sep 2016 • Couples
First off... I live in the Glenwood villas so this restaurant is a regular for me and my gf especially when we can't be bothered cooking. Yes, the restaurant is obviously very conveniently located for us but we would not keep coming back if it was bad.

First off the quality of all our meals thus far (and it's been numerous) has been of very good quality, I often comment how pleasantly surprised I am with the quality. Also the food is always well presented. 

Another nice surprise is only once have they not had something on the menu we wanted. Now, for those of you who live in VN you will know how rare this is. It is often a point of frustration with me that many restaurants I go to a give quite a bit of thought into what I order only to be told it's not available, so this restaurant is a breath of fresh air in that regard.

The prices are very reasonable, yes more than a typical vietnamese restaurant but well within most peoples budget. 

The service is good, and that too can be a bit of a rarity. Not once have I experienced the type of service the first reviewer of this place experienced. 

The decor and ambiance is ok, with enough variety of seating to satisfy most and they will alway adjust the air con or music level to what we ask.

All in all we feel lucky that right on our doorstep is a restaurant which provides good consistency and value for money.

stunningly poor
May 2016 • Friends
As you know l always have this urge to try new spots to report on, much to the discomfort of my friends who always want to go to their fave spots lol...

So l have passed this so called restaurant hundreds of times and have been curious. It looks okay from the outside. As l was lunching with a Vietnamese friend l recommended this and she was happy to try it out also.

Okay, basics first, District 2 is fast becoming overcrowded, dirty, congested, noisy, smelly and so on and so forth... mmnnn, traffic can be very bad at times so please give yourself the luxury of time or potentially be very late. Traffic across the bridge is relentless and unforgiving. Your problem there is that if is if you are lucky and get lighter traffic then you have time to kill before your booking. Also do not go if it is raining, that long main road consists of two parts Thao Dien Street which leads into Nguyen Van Huong Street, in which the restaurant is located. 

Normally this is not a problem, but having lived and worked in D2 for a year now, every time it rains it floods. The drains are so blocked water has no where to go, except on the roads lol. The last time it rained hard the water was over half way up to my knees. 

So, contras are traffic, location and weather. The restaurant itself is so so l guess. The air con must have been on maximum as l was so cold. Now l am a foreigner and we are usually always on the hot side lol but wah, l was shrammed. We moved tables but it was cold everywhere. Service was typical. staff shout at each other instead of actually going up to someone and actually talk to them. This is an issue that Vietnam seriously needs to get a grip on. We ordered smoothies to drink whilst the meal was being prepared. About five minutes later they trundle up and announce that they cant do what we ordered as they dont have ingredients. so we order another flavour. Five minutes later they trundle up and announce that the rain has manged to get through a leaky roof and all the sockets have no power... so no smoothies at all. Plan B was bottled water, safer and quicker we thought. Anyways, on with the tale.

We ordered some crab and noodle dish, pizza and soup and spring rolls. My friends are so patient and wonderful bless them. They have now grown accustomed to my doing some scientific experiments on their meals lol... l always take a few mouthfuls of each of their dishes so l can better report in more detail for your benefit.

Th soup was scalding hot (possibly only a microwave could do that much heat) and we had to leave it for about ten minuted before we could eat it. As we were already into our main course we left it. No loss really. My friend was the crab noodle thing. Which she about half of it. She is a seasoned fish and shellfish eater and she noted that the quality of the crab was poor, but would not let me kick off and replace it. The Vietnamese are sooooo not confrontational, it is a shame. I wish they would stand up for their rights as a consumer. But the reality is they they dont and service and quality are practically non existent across much of Vietnam.

Okay, l respect wish and we continue, l ordered a very hot pepperoni pizza with dry chillie powder as and extra.. its called Vesuvius or something so l was really excited and eager to try my dish. lt arrive nearly cold, the cheese was congealing and it had no more taste, flavour or strength than the soup. Very disappointing. Ah, the spring rolls, Dear me, what can l say that would be remotely polite, mmnnn 

Noe bear in mind that l have lived and worked in Indian, Chinese and Thai restaurants for years, so l have some understanding of operations and food etc.. I really really cannot begin to tell you what was in the spring rolls. A weird taste, try and see, let me know if you can guess the ingredients. l cant.

So, all in all a waste of time and money. prices are on the cheaper end of the spectrum but that is no excuse for poor standards.

So short answer is, go to D1 for food, wine etc. it is a million times better than anything l have thus far found in D2. l wish you well on your dinner search.
